content: The medication is indicated for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in patients aged 12 years and older with compensated liver disease. The recommended dosage is 25 mg orally once daily with food. Prior to initiating treatment, patients should be tested for HIV-1 infection, as tenofovir should not be used alone in patients co-infected with HIV. Baseline and periodic assessments of serum creatinine, phosphorus, estimated creatinine clearance (CrCl), urine glucose, and urine protein are recommended throughout treatment. For patients aged 6 years and older (weighing at least 25 kg) with compensated liver disease, the same dosage of 25 mg orally once daily with food is recommended. Safety and efficacy have not been established in patients under 6 years of age. Testing for HIV-1 infection is also required before starting treatment, and tenofovir should not be used alone in HIV co-infected patients. Regular monitoring of renal function and other parameters is advised. Certain drug interactions may alter the levels or effects of tenofovir alafenamide (AF). For example: Enasidenib: Increases tenofovir AF levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the dosage of sensitive substrates as per their prescribing information. Lenolisib: Avoid or use an alternative drug. Letermovir: Tenofovir AF decreases the effect of letermovir. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Sotorasib: Decreases tenofovir AF levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, refer to the prescribing information for dosage adjustments. Tepotinib: Increases tenofovir AF levels. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the dosage of P-glycoprotein (P-gp) substrates as recommended. Acalabrutinib: Increases tenofovir AF levels by inhibiting intestinal breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP). Use caution and monitor closely. Apalutamide: Decreases tenofovir AF levels by increasing elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. Berotralstat: Increases tenofovir AF levels via P-gp inhibition. Monitor or adjust the P-gp substrate dose if co-administered. Cabozantinib: Tenofovir AF increases cabozantinib levels, potentially leading to toxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. Danicopan: Increases tenofovir AF levels via P-gp inhibition. Consider dose reduction of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious adverse reactions. Darolutamide: Increases tenofovir AF levels by inhibiting BCRP. Avoid co-administration with BCRP inhibitors. If unavoidable, monitor closely and consider dose reduction of BCRP substrate drugs. Elagolix: Increases tenofovir AF levels via P-gp inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. Encorafenib: Increases tenofovir AF levels by inhibiting BCRP. Fostamatinib: Increases tenofovir AF levels by decreasing metabolism. Monitor for toxicities of BCRP substrate drugs and adjust dosages if necessary. Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir: Increases tenofovir AF levels by decreasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Ifosfamide: Co-administration with tenofovir AF may increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Monitor renal function and electrolytes closely. Istradefylline: Increases tenofovir AF levels via P-gp inhibition. Consider dose reduction of sensitive P-gp substrates. Lonafarnib: Increases tenofovir AF levels via P-gp inhibition. Monitor for adverse reactions and reduce P-gp substrate doses if needed. Mavorixafor: Increases tenofovir AF levels via P-gp inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. Momelotinib: Increases tenofovir AF toxicity by competing for plasma protein binding. Monitor closely and adjust doses of BCRP substrates as necessary. Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir: Increases tenofovir AF levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Orlistat: Decreases tenofovir AF levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and discontinue orlistat if virologic control is lost. Otesaconazole: Increases tenofovir AF levels by inhibiting BCRP. Use the lowest starting dose of BCRP substrates or reduce their dose. Regorafenib: Increases tenofovir AF levels by inhibiting BCRP. Safinamide: Increases tenofovir AF levels by inhibiting intestinal BCRP. Monitor for pharmacologic or adverse effects of BCRP substrates. Stiripentol: Increases tenofovir AF levels by inhibiting BCRP transport. Consider dosage reduction of BCRP substrates if adverse effects occur. Tafamidis: Increases tenofovir AF levels by inhibiting BCRP. Dosage adjustment of BCRP substrates may be necessary. Tucatinib: Increases tenofovir AF levels via P-gp inhibition. Consider reducing the dosage of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious toxicities. Vadadustat: Monitor for adverse effects and reduce substrate doses as needed. Voclosporin: Co-administration with tenofovir AF may increase nephrotoxicity. Monitor renal function closely. It is unknown if the drug is distributed in human breast milk. The benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother’s clinical need for the drug and potential adverse effects on the infant. Patients should be informed to take the medication with food on a regular dosing schedule and avoid missing doses to prevent resistance development. The medication should be stored at controlled room temperature (below 30°C or 86°F) in its original container with the lid tightly closed.
